A database running in level 90 (SQL 2005 mode) on a 2012 server will indeed reject PERCENTILE_CONT — the report's reasoning is technically correct. FreeTDS docs confirm TDS 7.0 corresponds natively to SQL Server 7.0 and that 7.4 is the native protocol for SQL 2012, BUT 7.0 CAN still connect to SQL 2012 (lower protocol just loses newer features). So 'TDS_VERSION=7.0 worked for the 2012 server on a non-standard port' is plausible/grounded, not a contradiction.
all_findings.note: Minor: 7.0 is a downgrade from the 2012-native 7.4, so describing it as 'required' likely means 'what made the FreeTDS connection succeed in their environment' rather than the protocol-optimal choice. The claim as written (it worked, baked into .env) is consistent with FreeTDS behavior.

all_findings.claim: CCPA acknowledge-within-10-business-days and substantive-response-within-45-days with a permitted single 45-day extension; TDPSA (Texas) effective 2024-07-01 with deletion right covering data 'provided by or obtained about' a consumer; GLBA data-level exemption from CCPA right-to-delete.

all_findings.note: All three legal assertions are accurate. all_findings.claim: Azure Synapse Serverless is pay-per-TB-scanned and cheaper than AWS Redshift Serverless, which carries an 8-RPU provisioned floor; AKS bills only cluster-hour meters with a free tier for non-prod (no per-vCPU node-management surcharge); DAS publishes CloudEvents 1.0 to Azure Event Grid.
all_findings.evidence: Synapse Serverless IS pay-per-TB-processed (~$5/TB read) — correct. AKS DOES bill only cluster-hour management meters with a Free tier (no fee, no SLA) for non-prod and charges only underlying VM/storage/network (no per-vCPU node-management surcharge) — correct. Event Grid natively supports publishing/consuming CloudEvents v1.0 JSON — the DAS-publishes-CloudEvents-1.0-to-Event-Grid pattern is technically supported (DAS-specific behavior itself not externally verifiable, but the capability is real). HOWEVER the '8-RPU provisioned floor' for Redshift Serverless is STALE: AWS introduced a 4-RPU minimum base-capacity option in June 2025 (expanded to more regions Nov 2025 and May 2026). 8 RPU is no longer the floor in supported regions.
all_findings.note: Bundle is mostly grounded but the load-bearing '8-RPU floor' comparison point is outdated as of 2025-06. The Synapse-cheaper-than-Redshift conclusion may still hold but the stated rationale (8-RPU floor) overstates Redshift's minimum; a 4-RPU floor narrows the gap. Recommend updating to 4-RPU minimum and re-checking the cost-delta claim.

all_findings.claim: AWS DMS zero-ETL Redshift integration availability ('GA 2025-07-23, PG 15.4+') and Fabric mirroring for PG Flex GA as the Azure analog — vendor capability/date claims underpinning the architecture summary.

all_findings.note: Both anchor capabilities verified to the date and version. The only nuance: Fabric PG-Flex mirroring GA was announced at Ignite 2025 (later than the AWS GA), and Fabric supports PG 14+, vs RDS zero-ETL's 15.4+ — fine for the architecture's portability argument. Solid foundation for the AWS-primary/Azure-portable design.

The record correctly tags these as 'ad-platform standard; design-proposed landing capture' / 'not yet in DAS docs', so the framing is honest — grounded with the caveat that 'documented vendor field' holds for the click-ID concept, not necessarily the exact CDP field label.
